findings.problems:
Reproduced every nous number on the live grid (azold-test-server:/home/azureuser/da-sgp/v5): byte-identical rent_occ_cost_psf==rent_resi_psf_med (hex8 625/625, max abs diff 0.0, 0 differ; +5 hdb_estimate=630 total); source counts private_observed 625/none 561/hdb_estimate 5; spread p0 2.02/p50 4.41/p90 5.67/p99 6.91/max 8.17, max/min 4.05x; business coverage 72/227=31.7%; CBD vs heartland signal separation confirmed. URA datastores both LIVE and free: d_49962204... returns 162 records (3 localities x 54 quarters), 2025-Q3 = Orchard 8.59 / Central Area-Outside Orchard 4.59 / Outside Central Area 5.15 (exact string is "Central Area - Outside Orchard"), retail sub-index resource live (122 rows). The prototype composite reproduces the claimed acceptance numbers exactly (psf p0 3.58/p50 11.54/p90 29.94/max 38.0, ratio 10.62; Orchard 37.8, Downtown 37.8, Tampines 17.9, Woodlands 25.1, LCK 5.2). So the recipe's evidence is honest. BUT the recipe has 5 real defects:

(1) EMBEDDING LEAKAGE — THE BIG ONE. The recipe asserts "rent/footfall must NOT become embedding inputs" but the e1 256d encoder (embedding/prep_features.py) selects features by a numeric-only blacklist: EXCLUDE_PREFIX = (cap_, colo_fit_, roi_, parent_, zone_type, ...) which does NOT exclude rent_; and VIEWS line 41 explicitly assigns prefix "rent_" to the PRICE view as an ENCODER INPUT. Therefore every new numeric rent_retail_psf_est/psm_est/confidence/n_obs_locality column is AUTO-SWEPT into the encoder. The new layer leaks straight into e1 unless prep_features.py EXCLUDE_PREFIX is patched to add ("rent_retail_",) OR the cols are excluded. The recipe is silent on this and would violate its own no-leak rule.

(2) PROBE-TARGET LEAKAGE via od_throughput. prep_features.py keeps od_throughput OUT of X precisely because it is a held-out probe target (labels.tgt_od_throughput). STEP B "Optional secondary: ... od_throughput" would fold a probe target into a PRICE-view input, contaminating eval #4 (probe sanity). od_throughput MUST NOT be used in the composite.

(3) COLLINEARITY / DOUBLE-COUNT. corr(vis_exit_footfall, retail_footfall_score)=0.857 on the live grid — two of the five composite terms (combined weight 0.35) measure nearly the same thing, over-weighting station/exit footfall. This is the root cause of the admitted Woodlands>Tampines inversion (Woodlands 25.1 > Tampines 17.9): Causeway checkpoint vis_exit_footfall inflates a heartland town above a true regional retail centre. Also TUAS (industrial port, 91 cells) lands at 12.8 psf — higher than many residential heartland subzones — because industrial/port footfall leaks into "retail" rent. The composite conflates throughput with retail demand.

(4) HEX9 CANNOT BE COMPUTED AS WRITTEN. Recipe says produce cols "at hex8+hex9" from "all already in master" signals, but hex9_all_features.parquet (7318x597) is MISSING retail_footfall_score, vis_exit_footfall, AND iso_walk10_spend (only nl_commercial_indicator + commercial_intensity present). 3 of 5 inputs absent at hex9. hex9 rent_retail_* must be INHERITED from parent_hex8 (col exists), not recomputed. Recipe's STEP B implies recomputation and would fail or silently produce a degenerate 2-term composite at hex9.

(5) CALIBRATION/SCALE is editorial, not data-grounded. The 3.5*exp(p*ln(38/3.5)) map is anchored to "published benchmarks ~25-40" the builder invents, while the only OBSERVED retail anchors (URA 8.59/4.59/5.15 psf/mo) are 4-5x LOWER than the prototype's Orchard 37.8. The recipe candidly flags this and defaults to "ground-floor scale, URA validates ORDERING only" — defensible, but it means the headline psf numbers are NOT observed and must be labeled an estimate/index, with rent_retail_confidence never "high" purely on the basis of the scale. Minor: 373 duplicate composite ranks create psf plateaus across low-signal heartland (cosmetic, rank(pct) handles it).

Non-problems I checked and cleared: numerical stability fine (comp min 0.008, no zero-comp cells, exp well-defined, fillna(0) safe); NA rule maps 471/1191 cells to NaN coherently (BUT note zone_type for ORCHARD is "residential" — the zone_type taxonomy is residential/industrial/nature, NOT retail-aware, so NA exclusion via zone_type is fine but tier/locality mapping correctly uses parent_pa, never zone_type); rename of rent_occ_cost_source has no runtime consumer (only build_hdb_rent_est.py, catalog JSON/MD, checkpoint docs) so it is safe but requires catalog regeneration; subzone agg gives 270 subzones psf 3.6-38.0 as claimed.</problems>

Consequences: (a) zone_type carries geographic context (airport/islands/industrial) that dominant_use cannot recover, so cells the original heuristic could not place were dumped into 'unknown' (247 of them — island clusters, Tuas/Pioneer port-industrial, Changi airport, water catchments); (b) dominant_use=='transport' is a single bucket that conflates non-leasable airside/port interiors (lu_transport_pct>=0.8, median walk-shed pop/spend/places all 0) with MRT-station retail frontage (median pop 90, spend 22, places 48) -> any retail/footfall model treats them identically; (c) Sentosa inherited the blanket SOUTHERN ISLANDS -> islands_restricted/unknown label even though it is a real F&B/retail/resort destination, so its frontage reads as 0 footfall and gets gated out of scoring.

findings.evidence_reproduced: Builder formula (build_retail_pack_sgp.py line 23-24) confirmed EXACTLY: retail_footfall_score = score100(0.6*minmax(vis_exit_footfall) + 0.4*minmax(dt_pop)). Note score100() itself re-applies minmax(1-99 pctile winsor)*100, so it is effectively a double-minmax of that blend. Coverage: vis_exit_footfall>0 for exactly 156/1191 hex8 = 13.1% (matches "13%"). Spearman vs dt_pop (my computation, n=1191): vis_exit_footfall +0.446 (LOWEST), retail_footfall_score +0.898, iso_transit15_pop +0.882, iso_walk10_pop +0.879, od_throughput +0.877, ca_footfall +0.877 — all match the evidence. Failure cells reproduced EXACTLY: dead PORT hex8 886520d811fffff (dominant_use=transport): dt_pop=6.11, od_throughput=0, vis_exit_footfall=12308.77 (phantom MRT/LRT exit taps), retail_footfall_score=41. findings.root_cause: retail_footfall_score puts 60% weight on vis_exit_footfall, a transit-exit POINT-SOURCE proxy (weekday tap counts mapped to the nearest MRT/LRT exit within 400m). It is structurally 0 for any hex without a rail station nearby (87% of all hex8), so it cannot represent pedestrian/general footfall. Worse, where it IS non-zero it dominates: a station-adjacent but economically dead cell (PORT, dt_pop=6) inherits a large phantom value, while genuine high-activity, high-throughput cells with no station exit (NASSIM dt_pop=6702/od=436k; Orchard Boulevard; Kampong Bugis) are crushed. The 0.4*dt_pop term cannot rescue them because of the 0.6 station weight. vis_exit_footfall is also the worst general-activity proxy available (Spearman to dt_pop only +0.446 vs +0.88 for every modeled-activity alternative). There is no real ground-truth pedestrian footfall layer in the atlas; vis_exit_footfall was a stopgap that got over-weighted.
findings.fix_recipe: REBUILD retail_footfall_score from modeled general activity, dropping vis_exit_footfall entirely. In build_retail_pack_sgp.py replace the o["retail_footfall_score"] line with a rank-blend. Exact recipe (verified on live grid): (1) For each input apply log1p then percentile-rank: def rank01(s): return np.log1p(pd.to_numeric(s,errors="coerce").fillna(0).clip(lower=0)).rank(pct=True). log1p tames the heavy tails (od_throughput max 5.9M, dt_pop max 88k); pct-rank makes inputs comparable and avoids the 1-99 winsor clipping that score100/minmax impose. (2) blend = 0.40*rank01(dt_pop) + 0.25*rank01(od_throughput) + 0.20*rank01(iso_walk10_pop) + 0.15*rank01(iso_transit15_pop). Weights: daytime presence is the primary footfall driver (0.40); through-movement OD (0.25); walkable catchment (0.20); transit-15min catchment (0.15). (3) Rescale to 0-100 over its own observed range: new = ((blend-blend.min())/(blend.max()-blend.min())*100).round().astype(int)  (or reuse score100 — but prefer this linear rescale to keep the rank ordering exact). (4) NA-gate, do NOT zero-score: set retail_footfall_score = NaN where zone_type in {nature, islands_restricted, islands_resort, water, unknown} OR dominant_use in {open_space, reserve, water} (consistent with the established zone_type NA treatment). This also cleanly removes the dead PORT cell's residual leakage (dominant_use=transport, dt_pop<50 — optionally extend NA-gate to transport/utility dominant_use with dt_pop<50). Do NOT touch format_fit_score's separate use of vis_exit_footfall in this audit item.

So site-finding on hex9 has zero native reach/footfall/competition signal and must inherit the smeared parent_hex8 value. CRITICAL FINDING in builders: build_iso_walk.py already distributes demand at HEX9 grain onto OSM walk-network nodes (node_h9 via h3.latlng_to_cell res 9) and snaps places at point grain; the ONLY hex8-specific input is the activity ORIGIN (mean of a hex8's places' coords, fallback pop-weighted hex9 centroid) and the output key. All native inputs exist at hex9: hex9_universe.parquet has lat/lng (7318 rows), hex9_population.parquet has pop_resident, places/sgp_places_final.parquet already carries hex9_id (190,591 places). build_iso_transit.py caches a full origin->hex9 minute matrix and explicitly states hex9 demand quantization is fine for transit reach. retail_footfall_score / industrial_adjacency_score / format_fit_score etc. are DOWNSTREAM composites of iso_*/dt_pop/vis_exit_footfall (verified in build_retail_pack_sgp.py and build_domain_primitives_sgp.py). dt_pop depends on hex8_od_features.parquet, and build_od_hex8.py maps LTA OD from BusStopCode/train PT_CODE to hex8 (H3 res 8) — bus-stop grain cannot be disaggregated below hex8, so OD/dt_pop is structurally hex8-only.
findings.root_cause: The whole iso/footfall/OD/site-finding pack was authored hex8-only (origins iterated over the 1,191-row hex8_universe; outputs keyed hex8_id) and folded into the hex8 master; hex9 was only ever a population/land-use/places carrier. hex9 therefore has the raw ingredients (its own pop, places via hex9_id, OSM walk graph, GTFS) but no builder loops over hex9 origins, so every reach/footfall/competition feature is missing and is reconstructed at query time by joining parent_hex8 — i.e. all 7 hex9 children of a hex8 receive the SAME smeared catchment value. This is fine for slowly-varying multi-km transit/OD/zone_type but wrong for the 800 m walk catchment and the micro footfall/competition signals that drive site selection, where a 460 m (hex9 edge) shift materially changes reach. Two distinct causes: (a) iso_walk10_*/severance/snap and the place-grain supply signals are genuinely finer than hex9 and were simply never run at hex9 origins (recompute is correct); (b) od_*/dt_pop/iso_transit15_*/zone_type derive from inputs that live at hex8-or-coarser grain (LTA OD at bus-stop->hex8, PA->SZ->hex8 zone classification), so they are inherently inheritance contracts.
findings.fix_recipe:
Split into NATIVE-RECOMPUTE vs DOCUMENTED-INHERIT.

NATIVE RECOMPUTE at hex9 (genuinely sub-hex8 signal; inputs all exist):
1. iso_walk10_* family (12 cols) + iso_euclid800_pop + iso_severance_ratio + iso_snap_dist_m + iso_reached_node_n. Generalize build_iso_walk.py: parameterize RES and the origin/universe source. Set RES=9; origin per hex9 = mean of that hex9's places' coords (places already have hex9_id) > pop-weighted child-centroid (hex9 is the leaf so just its own lat/lng) > geometric hex9 centroid from hex9_universe.parquet. Demand-node distribution is ALREADY hex9-grain (node_h9 = res-9 cell of each node), so leave it unchanged; the unserved/euclid/severance math is origin-keyed and needs no change. Loop Dijkstra over the 7,318 hex9 origins instead of 1,191 (~6x origins; same graph; est wall-clock ~6x the hex8 run, low risk, embarrassingly parallel by chunk). Output hex/hex9_iso_walk.parquet keyed hex9_id.
2. vis_exit_footfall + vis_main_road_m + vis_traffic_pass_proxy + vis_corner_premium (build_visibility.py): same pattern — swap the hex8 activity origin for the hex9 origin, station-exit/road inputs are point/segment grain. Output hex/hex9_visibility.parquet.
3. min15_* family (10 cols) + walk-amenity/place-count reach: recompute on hex9 origins (place supply is point grain, already hex9-aware).
4. Re-run the pack builders (build_retail_pack_sgp.py, build_domain_primitives_sgp.py) against a hex9 master so retail_footfall_score, industrial_adjacency_score, format_fit_score, retail_competition_pressure, commercial_activity_index, etc. fall out natively (they are pure functions of the recomputed iso_*/vis_*/dt_pop primitives — no new data).

DOCUMENT AS HEX8 INHERITANCE CONTRACT (input grain is hex8-or-coarser; native recompute impossible without new data):
- od_* (all 16: in/out/am/pm/throughput/self_containment/entropy/net_flow/...) and dt_pop/dt_pop_unadj/dt_ratio/dt_class/dt_clipped/dt_inflow/outflow/net — LTA OD is bus-stop->hex8 (build_od_hex8.py line 43 h3 res 8); cannot disaggregate below hex8.
- iso_transit15_* (4) and mrt_reach_*, time_to_*_min, labor_*, jobs_reach_45m, n_dest_* — multi-km transit reach; builder itself documents hex9 demand quantization is acceptable; inherit parent_hex8 value.
- zone_type, zone_type_broad — categorical PA->SZ->hex8 propagation; hex9 already has parent_pa/parent_subzone/parent_region, so inherit via parent_hex8 (or re-propagate from parent_subzone directly — identical result).
- adq_* equity/availability scores — derived from the above; inherit.

Implement the inheritance contract explicitly: in the hex9 master build, add an INHERITED_FROM_HEX8 manifest and do an explicit left-join hex9.parent_hex8 -> hex8[inherited_cols], with a boolean is_inherited_hex8 flag column per family (or a single inherited-cols list in the build report) so downstream consumers know which hex9 columns are smeared vs native. Add a `granularity` tag in build_catalog.py per column ('native_hex9' | 'inherited_hex8').
findings.acceptance_check: After build, hex9_all_features.parquet must contain all iso_walk10_*/vis_*/min15_* + recomputed footfall/industrial scores as NATIVE (non-null for non-water/non-reserve hexes), present-and-native count >= 36 of the listed cols. Concrete numeric gates: (1) WITHIN-PARENT VARIANCE — for the 7 hex9 children of each populated hex8, native iso_walk10_pop must vary: median coefficient of variation across sibling groups > 0.10 (proves de-smearing; a pure inherited join gives CV=0). (2) CONSERVATION — population-weighted mean of native hex9 iso_walk10_pop within a parent should be within +/-25% of the parent hex8 iso_walk10_pop (catchments overlap, so not exact, but same order). (3) SEVERANCE SANITY — median hex9 iso_severance_ratio in 0.35-0.65 band (matches hex8 builder's ~0.55 ideal-grid expectation; report median for both). (4) COVERAGE — populated hex9 (pop_resident>0) with iso_reached_node_n>0 >= 99% (matches hex8 builder's populated-hex-with-node check). (5) INHERIT MANIFEST — od_*/dt_pop/iso_transit15_*/zone_type carry is_inherited_hex8=True and are byte-identical to parent_hex8 value (group-by parent_hex8 nunique==1). (6) SPOT-CHECK — Toa Payoh Central hex9 children show non-uniform iso_walk10_pop (the builder docstring's canonical de-smearing case).
findings.external_data_needed: None for the native-recompute set (iso_walk10_*, vis_*, min15_*, and the downstream footfall/industrial/retail scores) — all inputs exist on the live grid: data/roads/roads.geojson (OSM walk graph), places/sgp_places_final.parquet (190,591 places already keyed with hex9_id), hex/hex9_universe.parquet (lat/lng), hex/hex9_population.parquet (pop_resident), data/gtfs/singapore-gtfs, and the LTA per-station taps file used by build_visibility.py. No purchase/download required. The INHERIT set (od_*/dt_pop/iso_transit15_*/zone_type/adq_*) is bounded by input grain, not by missing files — LTA origin_destination_bus/train CSVs are published only at bus-stop / station-code level, which cannot be disaggregated below hex8; obtaining finer OD would require non-public telco/farecard mobility data (paid, not currently held). Hence those are documented as an inheritance contract rather than recomputed.
findings.risk: (1) Compute: 7,318 hex9 Dijkstra origins vs 1,191 hex8 (~6x) on the same OSM graph — minutes-scale, parallelizable, low risk. (2) Sparse-supply hex9: many hex9 cells have 0 native places, so their activity-origin falls back to the hex9 geometric centroid (places-mean fallback chain in the builder handles this) — acceptable but the origin definition shifts slightly vs hex8; document it. (3) Catchment overlap: adjacent hex9 walk catchments overlap heavily (800 m >> 460 m hex9 edge), so summing children will exceed the parent — this is correct (per-origin reach, not a partition) but consumers must not treat iso_walk10_pop as additive across hex9. (4) Severance/euclid baseline uses the same node field — fine, but the euclid800 ball-point query at 7,318 origins is the slow inner loop; keep the cKDTree. (5) Double-source risk: if downstream code currently reads hex9 reach via parent_hex8 join, switching to native columns changes values app-wide — must bump a version and re-run any cached site-selection scores. (6) Inheritance honesty: the biggest correctness risk is leaving od_*/dt_pop SILENTLY smeared without the is_inherited_hex8 flag — site-finding consumers could mistake an inherited hex8 footfall for a native hex9 measurement; the manifest/granularity tag is the mitigation and should be mandatory, not optional. (7) zone_type re-propagation must match the PA->SZ->hex8 Not-Applicable treatment exactly (non-residential PAs not scored) or hex9 adequacy will diverge from hex8.
